title: Vetra Studio runs locally through the vetra CLI with your own Anthropic API key on three fixed ports
content:
## No invite code needed

The hosted Vetra Studio is gated behind an early-access code, but the same agent ships as a CLI you run yourself. The trade is the API key: locally you bring your own **Anthropic API key**, because the agent runs on Claude. Prerequisites are Node ≥ 24 on macOS or Linux; pnpm is optional (the installer uses it if present, offers to install it, else falls back to npm).

Two install paths:

```bash
# A — installer script (sets up both the `ph` and `vetra` CLIs)
curl -fsSL https://get.vetra.io | sh

# B — straight from the Vetra registry, nothing piped to a shell
npm install -g ph-cmd vetra-cli --registry=https://registry.vetra.io
pnpm add -g ph-cmd vetra-cli --registry=https://registry.vetra.io
```

If you want to read the script first, `curl -fsSL https://get.vetra.io -o install-vetra.sh`, inspect, then `sh install-vetra.sh`. The first launch walks Claude auth, then prints the Studio URL — open `http://localhost:8090/`. Re-start any time with `vetra`.

From source: clone `powerhouse-inc/vetra-cli`, `pnpm install`, `pnpm dev` for the interactive agent REPL with an embedded Reactor and Switchboard, exporting `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...` once. When the agent starts a build the logs print `Vetra Studio: http://localhost:8090/d/<driveId>`. `pnpm dev:reset` wipes the local dev workspace.

## Three ports, no fallback

A single `vetra` process runs the REPL plus an embedded Reactor and Switchboard, and it reserves three ports **with no fallback** — free them first or startup fails:

| Service | Port | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vetra Studio (proxy) | 8090 | Browser entry point, the URL you open |
| Connect | 27370 | Editor front-end |
| Switchboard | 59220 | GraphQL API |

These are deliberately unusual numbers so they do not collide with the ordinary Powerhouse dev ports — `ph vetra` puts Connect on 3001 and Switchboard on 4001, and `ph connect studio` uses 3000. Running `vetra` and `ph vetra` side by side is therefore fine.

_Source: `apps/academy/docs/academy/01-GetStarted/00-VetraStudio.md` (Running Vetra Studio locally), Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45._
description: Install via curl -fsSL https://get.vetra.io | sh, or npm i -g ph-cmd vetra-cli --registry=https://registry.vetra.io. One process reserves 8090, 27370 and 59220.
